rows.question: What was the LUCI flame spreading over in the fabric test?
rows.answer:
LUCI burned 5 × 30 cm cotton–fiberglass fabric downward in simulated lunar gravity. Its flame base advanced at 0.9 mm/s versus 1.5 at 1 g, and its tip at 1.1 versus 2.8 mm/s. Fabric extinction occurred about 45 seconds later in the partial-gravity run. [1]

1. LUCI, slower spread and a longer-lived SIBAL flame. In the New Shepard flight a 5 × 30 cm cotton–fiberglass strip burned downward, while a 4 mm PMMA rod burned upward. The apparatus rotated and both samples used the same atmosphere. For SIBAL, the paired ground/partial-g comparisons report flame-base speeds of 1.5/0.9 mm/s and flame-tip speeds of 2.8/1.1 mm/s. The flame-width comparison reports extinction roughly 45 seconds earlier on Earth. The individual flight fit gives 0.92 mm/s for the base and the comparison table rounds to 0.9. The rocket carried the experiment in a sealed chamber in simulated lunar gravity. The deck’s total burn duration across the experiment is a poor substitute for a specific fabric’s duration. [2]

rows.answer:

Particles from overheated materials have different size distributions. The experiments measured the signal against defined thresholds, with no single response representing every material. [2]

rows.question: How many burns were planned in the 2026 FM² design?
rows.answer:
FM² refreshes the chamber between burns; oxygen can fall during a burn. Initial oxygen, successful ignition, post-igniter spread and oxygen at extinction are different measurements. [1]

7. FM², prediction with four dependent trials. The March 2026 design supersedes a 2024 configuration involving two different fuels. On viewer p. 10 it specifies Synergy Pro Navy; the older shortlist table on viewer p. 14 calls one candidate Natural Synergy Pro. Confirm grade, finish and lot before joining a comparison. With a nominally common limiting oxygen concentration for the four specimens, outcomes are dependent and the effective sample size is small. A Brier score can compare predictions on resolved indices. It cannot establish calibration from one four-burn mission. NASA gives qualitative expectations and a 24–26% expected LOC. The guide's 26%/1.5 percentage-point distribution is a teaching assumption. A shared oxygen threshold assumes that sufficient starting oxygen will produce sustained spread after a functioning igniter. Registering a separate ignition model would be necessary to estimate a distinct ignition-failure probability. A nominal attempt with no ignition and an invalid igniter have different scoring dispositions. A changed design or missing footage can also make an observation unscorable. The April FY 2027 budget request plans FM² lunar work for 2027. These documents provide the design and planning basis; an official result with traceable per-burn outcomes is still needed for scoring. [2]

rows.question: How long did the aircraft comparison observe the SIBAL sample?
rows.answer:

They strengthen the *early spread* comparison; their time windows cannot test a 45-second difference in extinction. An earlier poster describes immediate Earth extinction under its own conditions; use the actual paired LUCI run to answer the numerical duration question. [1]

A separate 20-second aircraft test matched the fuel, 5 cm width, direction, approximate gravity and initial atmosphere. It measured base spread of 0.86 mm/s versus 0.92 on LUCI. The centrifuge drop test reported 1.1 mm/s. [2]
